segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Aakashwani and I am Vilsa Williams with the Midday News.
The headlines.
From Minister Narendra Modi stresses the need to unite society against divisive forces to build a developed India by 2047.
Inaugurates Chinmay Amrit Mahotsav Global Semelan at Bharat Mandapam.
The government extends duty-free import deadline for one million tons of raw sugar to 31 December.
Allahabad High Court rules survivor of sexual assault under POXO Act eligible for compensation
despite no physical injuries.
India criticizes Pakistan over religious freedom and protection of minorities, says Islamabad
had no standing to lecture India.
India. Low-pressure forms over Bay of Bengal may develop into cyclonic storm. IMD predicts
rainfall activities in coastal Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh.
And in Asian Paragames, Parashute Monagarwal sets new world record, winning two gold medals
in women's 50-meter rifle-three positions.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said the youth have always remained at the center
of his government's policies and initiatives. Inoculating the Chinmay Amrit Mahotsav Global
Samaelan at Bharat Mandapur, New Delhi today, Mr. Modi said for the past 25 years he has
been serving the nation to the best of his ability as head of the government.
The government has introduced the national education policy to align the country's education
system with the needs of a new India.
He added that the policy emphasizes India's rich traditions and knowledge, imparting education
in mother tongue, modern science and emerging technologies.
and new technology. All of this has been given importance.
Prime Minister Modi said all institutions must work towards the common goals of national
development and scaling the country's pride. He stressed the need to unite society against
divisive forces, promote self-reliance and involve every citizen in the resolve to
build developed India by 2047.
The government has extended the duty-free import deadline for one million tons of raw sugar
sugar, under the tariff rate quota to 31 December. This step has been taken to boost domestic
supplies of sugar during the festive season. According to a notification issued by the
Finance Ministry, the import window has been extended till 31 December this year. Earlier
the government had allowed imports of 1 million tons of raw sugar until 31 this month.
The Allahabad High Court has ruled that a survivor of sexual assault under the Poxo
Act cannot be denied compensation merely because the medical report does not record physical
injuries.
A division bench of Justice Shekhar B. Sarraf and Justice Amitabh Kumar Rai directed authorities
to pay 3 lakh rupees to a minor under the Uttar Pradesh Rani Lakshmi Bhai Mahila Samman
Kosh scheme within 10 days of submission of a certified copy of the order.
The court set aside the district steering committee's decision to withhold compensation
observing that physical injuries are not a necessary condition for establishing
penetrative sexual assault under Section 3 of the Boxer Act. It held that the
absence of injury marks cannot by itself negate an allegation of sexual assault.
The bench noted that once the FIR and charge sheet indicate an offense
under Section 4 of the Act, compensation cannot be denied solely on the basis of
a medical report that requires no injuries. India has criticised Pakistan
Pakistan at the United Nations over religious freedom and protection of minorities.
First secretary at India's permanent mission to the UN, Bhavika Mangalan, then said their
numbers were declining and their rights were regularly abused.
She said a country unable to ensure the safety of its own minorities had no standing to
lecture India, and urged Pakistan to focus on developments in areas of Jammu and Kashmir
under its illegal occupation, including Ravla court. Recalling its refusal to
acknowledge the bodies of its soldiers killed during the 1999 Kargil war while
raising concerns over its remarks on religious freedom and burial rights. She
said the Indian army had buried several Pakistani soldiers with military
honors and in accordance with Islamic rights. Her remarks came during a
discussion on an interim report by UN Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion and belief,
Nazila Ghania, which raised concerns over alleged denial of funeral rights in Jammu and
Kashmir.
Let me remind them, it was an Indian army who buried a number of Pakistani soldiers
with military honors and in accordance with Islamic rights.
Pakistan's deep obsession with what is happening in the Indian Union territory of Jammu and
Kashmir should be actually directed at the developments that are underway in the
parts of Jammu and Kashmir under its legal occupation, such as Rawalakot.
In Pakistan, a number of minorities are shrinking, their rights regularly abused.
A state that cannot ensure the safety of its own minorities has no standing to lecture India.
India has said the United Nations is losing its legitimacy as the outcome of a war fought
eight decades ago continues to shape the composition of the UN Security Council.
India has called for reforms to make the Council more representative and reflective
of contemporary global realities.
Addressing the UN General Assembly yesterday,
India's permanent representative
to the United Nations, B. Harish said,
no war fought over 80 years ago
should determine the present-day world order.
The authority derived from a victory eight decades ago
cannot compensate for the deficit
in legitimacy of an unrepresentative
security council today.
An organization that cannot renew its principal organ
will find it ever harder to command authority
in a world that has moved beyond 1945.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Stay connected with AIR News, Follow us on X at AIR News Alerts and visit newsaunair.gov.in
for the latest updates.
Welcome back to the midday news.
Minority Affairs Minister Kiran Rajiju has said the government is proactively addressing
addressing the issues and concerns of Indian citizens. In a social media post, Mr. Rijiju
said the stranded Umrah pilgrims have returned safely to India. He added that more than 10,000
normal Umrah pilgrims had also returned to India earlier, while efforts are underway
to assist the remaining pilgrims.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today attended the Army Commanders Conference in New Delhi,
The three-day conference, which began on Wednesday, has brought together the Army's senior leadership
to discuss the evolving security environment, operational preparedness, capability development
and the modernization of the force.
On the occasion, Mr Singh released the Land-Warfare Doctrine, which will provide an overarching
framework to prepare the Indian Army to meet the challenges posed by the evolving character
of warfare and future conflicts.
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitaraman is chairing the 30th meeting of the Financial
Stability and Development Council, FSDC, in New Delhi. The meeting is being attended by
Chief Economic Advisor Dr. V. Ananta Nageswaran, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, Secretary of
Electronics and IT Ministry S. Krishnan, and Chairpersons of Insurance, Regulatory
and Development Authority of India.
Voting has begun for 11 MLC Seeds in Uttar Pradesh, 8 in Bihar, 5 in Maharashtra and 4 in Karnataka.
Polling is underway and will continue till 4 p.m. The voting is taking place for the biennial elections
to the Legislative Council from graduate and teachers constituencies in these four states.
Counting of votes will take place on October 27.
The enforcement directorate ED is conducting search operations at 13 locations across
Delhi, NCR, Bengaluru and Tendigarh. Officials at the ED informed that the searches are in
connection with fraudulent NRI housing loans obtained using forged documents. The officials
added that entities covered in the probe include Antricks promoters and developers
birds private limited, and sunshine infra-well private limited, further details are awaited.
Two satellite-tagged Amur falcons, Appapang and Alang, have returned to Manipur after
travelling across 23 countries in Asia and Africa, marking the successful completion
of their nearly year-long tracking journey.
In a social media post, Union Environment Minister Pupendra Yadav said the birds
arrived in Manipur yesterday, 11 days after departing from their breeding grounds in North
Eastern China. He noted that the two Falcons were attacked by scientists of the Wildlife
Institute of India in November 2025. We have more from our correspondent.
The return of the Amafalcon marks the completion of a round-rape migration journey, highlighting
the remarkable long-distance movements of the migratory birds. The Falcons are
now expected to spend 2-3 weeks at select stopover sites in the mountainous areas of
Tamenglong district in Manipur. During this period, they will feed on termites
and build up essential fat reserves for their next migratory leg. From Manipur, the birds
are expected to undertake a 16-on-stop flight of nearly 6,000 km to Somalia,
including a challenging 3,000 km crossing of the Arabian Sea. The annual arrival of the
Amar falcon is eagerly awaited by local communities in Manipur who have played a significant role
in protecting the migratory birds.
Neethika Gupta, Akashwani News, Delhi
A low-pressure area has formed over the Bay of Bengal, raising the possibility of a cyclonic
storm over the coming days. The Indimitrological Department has forecast gradual intensification
and west-northwestward movement towards the North Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South
Odisha coast, the system's exact track and potential impact will become clearer as it
develops, more from our correspondent.
A low-pressure area has formed over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal, raising
the possibility of a cyclonic storm along the eastern coast.
According to the India Meteorological Department, IMD, the system is likely to intensify
into a depression by tomorrow, a deep depression by the day after tomorrow, and a cyclonic
storm by this Monday morning.
moving west, northwest wards, it is likely to approach the north, Andhra Pradesh and adjoining
south Odisha coasts over the following two days.
Odisha is likely to witness increased rainfall activity starting this Monday, with widespread
rain and isolated heavy rainfall expected between this Tuesday and Thursday.
The IMD has advised fishermen to follow weather warnings and avoid venturing into the affected
sea areas.
Rakaas Das for Rakaas Fani News, Bhuvaneswar.
IMD has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahi,
Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karayakal today. The Met Department also predicted heavy
rainfall over the Andhra, Bala and Nicobar Islands, Andhra Pradesh, coastal Karnataka and South
interior Karnataka. And Parashutra Monahagarwal produced a terrific performance setting a new
world record to win gold in the women's 50-metre rifle three positions SH1 competition
edition at the Asian Paragames, she shot .357.5 at the IEG Prefecture General Shooting Gallery
to set the new record and claim her second gold medal of the MEGA event.
Now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Prime Minister Narayan Ramo stresses the need to unite society against divisive forces
to build a developed India by 2047 inaugurates Chinmay Amrit Mahotsav Global Summelan at
Harat Mandapam. Government extends duty-free import deadline for 1 million tons of raw sugar
to 31 December. Allahabad High Court rules survivor of sexual assault under Boxer Act
eligible for compensation, despite no physical injuries. India criticizes Pakistan over
religious freedom and protection of minorities, says Islamabad had no standing to lecture
India. Low pressure forms over Bay of Bengal. May develop into Cyclonic Storm. IMD predicts
rainfall activities in coastal Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh. And in Asian Paragames,
Parashutamona Arbalwal sets new world record, winning two gold medals in women's 50-metre
rifle three positions.
With that, we end the midday news.
